brief: EUR and USD rates continued drifting wider last week (EUR 5-10bps, USD 15-20bps), pushing both to 10yr highs with vol on the higher side, after more than 60bps of widening over the past two months. Positioning in rates is now very short, which the author reads as skewing near-term risk toward a relief rally unless inflation surprises higher. Equities (SPX +1.2%, SX5E +1%, NDX +3.25%) held up on light investor positioning, and the author sees SPX building upside momentum, favoring SPX calls given low implied vol. Credit widened broadly, with EUR Senior Fins cash and AT1/Corp Hybrids underperforming and net issuance minus fund flows deteriorating. Still, the author argues equity resilience, the rates repricing already done, short rates positioning, and an expected October issuance slowdown should support credit into a 1-month horizon, with spreads now above their 70th percentile. Preferred trades: long EUR Senior Fins cash and Hyperscaler credit baskets, selling October iTraxx Main straddles, and shorting rich EUR BB credit. Separately, French OAT-Bund spreads widened past 110bps, now wider than iTraxx SubFin for the first time ever, favoring short risk SubFin against long risk OAT-Bund spreads.
